title: A hymn in Gauri
hook: Gauri holds Sukhmani and the Bavan Akhri

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raga Gauri, and your line was earnest and deep. Did you have one unhurried conversation? Today, two long compositions that live inside Gauri, and the end of the week. Day one thousand seventy-one.

Peace of mind has a name in the Guru Granth Sahib, and an address. The name is Sukhmani. The address is a heading on ang two hundred sixty-two: Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala five. A whole block of year two walked through it. But it's easy to forget the first word of that heading, the one a singer reads before anything else. Before it's Sukhmani, it's Gauri, the earnest raga you met yesterday. Today: a hymn in Gauri.
screen: `PEACE OF MIND HAS A NAME.` → `GAURI SUKHMANI, MAHALA FIVE.` → `BEFORE SUKHMANI, GAURI.`

segments.voice: Sukhmani is Guru Arjan's, and it's long: section after section, each opened by a salok. Its first ashtapadi begins with remembering. In paraphrase: remembering, remembering, I find peace. And its rahao says what the name means: Sukhmani, peace, the nectar of the Lord's Name, which comes to rest in the minds of devotees. So the composition defines itself. Now hear it as a Gauri hymn. Gauri is earnest, unhurried, leaning in close. A composition that wants to settle a restless mind, slowly, over a long stretch, is right at home in that sound. The raga gives Sukhmani its pace before the words give it its meaning. A few pages earlier in Gauri sits a different kind of long hymn, also Guru Arjan's: the Bavan Akhri. It walks through the letters of the alphabet one at a time, and for each letter it gives a teaching, the way a child might learn letters, a word for every sound. Kabir has a Bavan Akhri in Gauri too, further on in the section. So Gauri holds two of the Granth's patient shapes: peace, built section by section, and wisdom, built letter by letter. Both take time. Gauri gives them time. That's today's line: peace in gauri. And look back at the week. The order of the ragas, thirty-one moods. Sri Rag, the first raga, and its hymn, which watch now. Majh, punjabi longing, and its hymn, letters of longing. Gauri, earnest and deep, and today, peace in gauri. Tomorrow the list moves on to Asa.
screen: `SUKHMANI DEFINES ITSELF: PEACE, THE NAME.` · `GAURI GIVES IT ITS PACE.` · `THE BAVAN AKHRI: LETTER BY LETTER.` · then, large: `PEACE IN GAURI.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to one Gauri shabad. If you can, find a recording of the opening of Sukhmani, sung in Gauri, and let it play through the sit. Don't chase the meaning. Let the pace do its work. If you can't find one, take the first idea of Sukhmani and make it a breath: remembering on the way in, peace on the way out. Remembering. Peace. Let the rhythm be slower than feels natural, the way Gauri moves. When a thought pulls you away, come back to the next breath, as if starting the next section. If you pray, you can let the breath carry Waheguru instead. The bell holds the time.
A hymn in Gauri. Sukhmani, Guru Arjan's long hymn of peace, and the Bavan Akhri, teaching letter by letter, both set in Gauri's earnest pace. Today's word.
Your line: peace in gauri. Today, when the day speeds up, take one breath with the practice's two words: remembering on the way in, peace on the way out. Day one thousand seventy-one.

howItsDone: Sukhmani Sahib is recited in Sikh homes and gurdwaras, by individuals or by groups, and is also sung in kirtan in Raag Gauri; the Bavan Akhri is read as part of the Gauri section of the Guru Granth Sahib.

original.note: Gurmukhi: Sukhmani, Guru Arjan's hymn of peace in Raag Gauri.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sukhmani is a prayer on its own.
what it means: a long hymn of Guru Arjan set in Gauri, whose earnest pace suits a composition meant to settle the mind.

what a scholar hears: Sukhmani (Gauri Sukhmani M5, from Ang 262) is built of ashtapadis each opened by a salok, and its rahao glosses the title; nearby Guru Arjan's Bavan Akhri (Ang 250) and, later, Kabir's (Ang 340) are acrostics on the letters of the alphabet, all within the Gauri section.
